verdict.rationale: Sketch documents that its native .sketch file is a zipped archive of JSON data plus binary images, published openly on GitHub. Community users confirm this enables plugins and git workflows, and the sketchtool CLI can generate assets. That means design files are portable in an inspectable, open-ish format. However, nothing documents a bulk export of all account or Workspace data (comments, versions, library and workspace metadata) for leaving the service. Missing for 10: a documented full Workspace/account data export, an export path for cloud-side data such as comments and version history, and independent hands-on confirmation of a complete migration off Sketch.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Sketch stores documents in `.sketch` format, a zipped archive of JSON formatted data and binary data such as images.
Create assets with a single command with the Sketch command-line interface `sketchtool`.
The file format is basically zipped json files, so there's a robust plugin ecosystem and you can do things like git integration pretty easily.
